blocks.markdown: Research as of 12 November 2026. UK technology landscape, selected provider baselines, public customer/partner references and evidence-linked opportunity briefs for Flora. The selected landscape contains 80 provider views. Depth and evidence readiness vary; this is not a census, a supplier ranking or a validated canonical import.
# Delivery correction and acceptance criteria

The deliverable is one coherent UK Technology foundation, not a sequence of research updates. The current document is a working evidence collection. Profile headings and source links are not completed enterprise baselines. The earlier approximate completion percentages are retired until requirements are auditable.

Research completion and software integration are separate gates. Research can be complete while an import implementation is pending. Conversely, a technically valid import cannot make incomplete research complete.

| Gate | Required completed output |
| --- | --- |
| Industry understanding | Scope, segments, economic boundaries, value chain, capabilities, operating models and competitive structure |
| Population | Documented key-enterprise selection across every agreed segment, exclusions and overlap resolution |
| Enterprise understanding | A consistent baseline for each selected enterprise: identity, UK role, business/operating model, offerings, ecosystem, strategy and material change, each sourced or explicitly unavailable |
| Relationships | Products, partners and named customers with typed roles, scope, evidence attribution and dates/Unknowns |
| Opportunities | Evidence-linked business consequences, alternative explanations, potential interventions and validation questions |
| Evidence assurance | Atomic claims, source passages/locators, dates, scope, contradictions, permissions status and historical/current distinctions |
| Handover | Consolidated research, coverage matrix, open gaps and candidate import mapping without invented canonical IDs |

A field may close as unavailable only after an actual documented search; an unperformed task does not close as Unknown. No fabricated budgets, deployment status, private architecture or customer identity is allowed.
## Confirmed integration dependency

The inspected main-snapshot importer has a finite official-publisher allowlist that does not include most technology-provider domains. Therefore provider-page records cannot currently be called validated imports through that route. A later Codex integration task must review source-policy expansion, technology-domain registration and canonical identities through existing owners; this research task does not authorise weakening the gate.

The importer also requires actual source bytes/checksums or the separately supported honest reviewed-excerpt path. A Page link or prose paraphrase does not satisfy that contract. Source references gathered here must be converted into located atomic candidate records before technical validation.

Industry structure, an expanded 80-view selection, reference operating models and opportunity briefs are assembled below. # Scope and completion requirements

Cover UK-headquartered providers and international providers with evidenced UK operations. The foundation requires industry structure and economics; a justified key-enterprise population; comparable business/operating models; applications, technologies and partner links; dated customer relationships; change forces and opportunity hypotheses; and an evidence-backed import pack. Completion requires substantive coverage across these areas, not simply mentioning each segment. Unknown private facts are legitimate gaps; incomplete research is not completion.
The earlier 20% was an approximate planning judgement, not a measured score. No defensible 100% completion claim is made here.

# Economic anchors and measurement boundaries

The government’s June 2026 Digital and Technologies release estimates 107,082 companies, £408bn turnover, 1.33m employees and £158bn GVA for 2024. It uses a novel methodology and explicitly warns against treating it as the Digital Sector, the wider Digital Economy or a basis for direct international/SIC-sector comparison. Small firms account for most companies while large firms contribute most turnover. [D&T economic statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/digital-and-technologies-sector-statistics-volume-1-economic-statistics/digital-and-technologies-sector-economic-statistics).

The separate Digital Sector statistical series provisionally estimates £177.2bn GVA in 2024, 6.8% of UK GVA. This is a different definition, not an amount to add to the D&T measure. [Digital Sector statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/economic-estimates-digital-sector-annual-2010-to-2024-and-regional-2010-to-2022-gross-value-added/economic-estimates-digital-sector-annual-2010-to-2024-and-regional-2010-to-2022-gross-value-added).

The 2026 cyber study estimates 2,603 firms, £14.7bn annual sector revenue and 69,600 FTEs. AI, cyber, cloud and software populations overlap and must not be summed. [Cyber study](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/cyber-security-sectoral-analysis-2026/cyber-security-sectoral-analysis-2026).

# Competitive structure and opportunity hypotheses
The following are analytical interpretations, not verified buying opportunities.

| Structural feature | Interpretation | Research / customer validation question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Applications depend on data, infrastructure and implementation | Buying and delivery responsibility may span multiple providers | Who owns integration, operation and outcome accountability? |
| Technology firms are also technology buyers | Provider profiles can expose their own transformation needs | Which disclosed change programme has an unresolved requirement? |
| Multi-platform AI appears in customer disclosures | Governance and interoperability may matter alongside model choice | Where are data, controls and value measurement fragmented? |
| Sourcing revenue and service economics differ | High revenue growth may not imply stronger margins | Which segment and profit measures reflect economic value? |
| Acquisitions and disposals change provider boundaries | Historical relationships need effective dates | Is the named supplier still in the same group and delivery role? |
| Channel partners offer overlapping capabilities | Rivalry and collaboration can coexist | Is the relationship resale, implementation, operation or joint development? |
Prioritise hypotheses by evidence strength, business materiality, change timing, capability fit and unresolved validation needs. Do not score fictional budgets or infer procurement intent.

# FLORA modelling and import contract

Represent provider, legal entity, product, technology category, business capability, partner, customer and dated event separately. Each relationship carries source URL, passage locator, publication/event/retrieval dates, geography, fact/inference/scenario type, supplier/customer attribution, status and gaps. Acquisition relationships require effective dates.

Suggested relationship types: owns product, supports capability, declares alliance, implements, operates, resells, uses product, selected, announced rollout, reported go-live, historically owned and potentially relevant to. Do not collapse potential relevance into deployed use.

Views: industry landscape; enterprise operating model; provider/customer ecosystem; change timeline; ranked opportunity hypotheses. Public-source models must visibly distinguish published and inferred edges. Hypothetical architectures remain separate scenarios.

This Page is a research working pack, not a machine-validated import. Source-operation permissions and current canonical IDs must be reconciled before ingestion. No production or Pipeline records have been modified.

# Cloud competition evidence and segment implications

The CMA's final cloud investigation decision was published on 31 July 2025. Its summary reports £10.5bn of customer spending in 2024 and identifies significant barriers to entry, switching and expansion. Its provider-share ranges have a UK-plus-EEA geographic scope in the footnote and must not be labelled UK-only market shares. These are historical regulatory findings, not a 2026 supplier ranking. [Final summary, paragraphs 3–6 and 17–21](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/688b20e6ff8c05468cb7b120/summary_of_final_decision.pdf).

The foundation therefore distinguishes three forms of competition. Infrastructure platforms compete through service breadth, capital investment and ecosystem dependencies. Software vendors compete within business capabilities while depending on platforms and implementation partners. Delivery firms compete for transformation and operations work but can partner with those same vendors and with each other. This is an interpretation supported by the CMA investigation, declared partner roles and the named multivendor customer cases; it is not a calculated market-share model.

For Flora, the practical unit of analysis is the business capability and dated change programme. “Uses cloud” is too broad. “Aviva reports a claims/fraud data migration to Snowflake on AWS, with named delivery support” allows a defensible discussion of data operations, assurance and adoption without inventing its architecture or procurement intent.
